game.title: SNOW PATROL
game.pitch: You are Vince, twenty, long blonde hair with a bit of a curl, the newest hand on the Kessel Patrol. You run the mountain patrol for the Kessel valley: its slopes, its roads, its village and the people who get lost on it. You have a log station, a snowmobile, a helicopter, a pair of old skis, and Koda, a grey-and-white husky with one ear that never stands up.

collections.doc: What each rank opens, beyond the gear in the shops.
Old patrol badges hidden around the valley (enamel pins from the station's first fifty years).

Tannberg Village, the base area, is one planned town (see TOWN below): Main Street runs north from
the parking lot at the valley road up to the lift base plaza, with Patrol HQ and its vehicle yard on
the west side and Hollin, the guest village, on the east.
Spots where charges can go: the two weak zones and two that are fine.

Gentle tilted shelves shaped into steeper ground, where something has to be reachable:
the forested back side of the Tannberg, where skiers go when they should not.

Hollin, the guest village, and the buildings round the plaza: [x, z, rot, kind]. `rot` turns the
front (local +z) to face: -PI/2 faces west onto Main Street, PI/2 east, 0 south.
Signposts: where they stand on Main Street, and the districts their arms point to.

collections.doc:
Marked landing zones for the helicopter (orange-flagged rings on the snow): the patrol's own pad, and
the flats it uses on the ridges and at the huts.

unclassified.doc:
`ahead`: how far past the character the camera aims, as a share of its distance. Aiming past
you rather than at you puts you in the lower third and shows the ground you are heading into.
`portrait`: how much further back the camera sits on a tall, narrow phone screen.

Which slopes the wind loads. Snow blows over the ridge and settles in the lee, so the wind
that came with the new snow decides which of the four slopes carry slab. One of these per
reload, picked by the day.
The guns: where they stand and how far they reach (m).
Multipliers on the light that falls on snow (linear rgb): [lit, shade].

The people's night light (Field Guide Alpine, src/render/fieldGuide.ts): a cold fill on their colours
and a rim from the sky round their edges, both zero by day, so at night a figure stays readable
against moonlit snow without the night itself getting any brighter. Set by the rig.

Each piece's footprint (its own frame, metres) and how it meets the ground. `rules` say what ground it
can stand on when its spot is chosen; `drape` is how high (local y) the ground snow it carries reaches:
those parts are laid onto the terrain under them rather than left flat.

The ground: snow that is a little blue in the shade and warm in the sun, wind-scoured rock on
the steeps, packed roads, groomed pistes and the lake's grey ice. Drawn in chunks so the ones
behind you are culled; a ring of far peaks closes the valley.
Hand-placed patrol props: a rescue toboggan at the station, the lift top and the base; rescue caches where trouble happens; lanterns by doors.
Where things are inside and around the station.

limitations.text: No enemy or encounter configuration was found as data.
Behaviour that exists only in code (AI, spawn logic, physics) is not executed or simulated by DESIGNCRAFT; it is visible only through PLAYCRAFT evidence when present.

missions.title: Morning Rounds
missions.brief: The weather station up on Grauhorn Pass went quiet overnight. Take the sled up the pass road and get it talking again. Koda will want to come.
missions.alert: The Grauhorn weather station stopped transmitting overnight.
missions.done: Station is transmitting again. Thanks. Fresh numbers: forty centimetres overnight up there.

objectives.text: Say good morning to Koda
Get on the sled in the garage
Ride up the pass road to the weather station
Clear the ice off the station and restart it
Head home to the station

missions.title: Eyes on Kessel Bowl
missions.brief: Forty centimetres of new snow and a west wind overnight. Fly over Kessel Bowl, above the pass road, and find out which of its four slopes are loaded. Nose on each slope, low and close, and the scanner reads it.
missions.alert: Heavy loading reported above the pass road. Recon flight requested.
missions.done: Report filed. Slopes A and C are loaded. We bring them down tomorrow, or today if you are up for it.

objectives.text: Start the helicopter on the pad
Fly to Kessel Bowl
Scan the four slopes: nose on each one, close and low
Fly home and land on the pad

missions.title: Controlled Release
missions.brief: Slopes A and C are wind slab on a weak layer. Close the pass road, climb to Kessel Ridge, set a charge on each loaded slope, get clear and fire. The berm in the runout is there to catch it.
missions.alert: Slopes A and C above the pass road are ready to go. Bring them down on our terms.
missions.done: Clean release, the berm held, the road is open. That is how it is done.

objectives.text: Take the charges from the locker in the garage
Close the pass road at the barrier
Take the ridge track up to Kessel Ridge
Set a charge on each loaded slope
Get clear of the slope, then fire the charges
Watch it run
Reopen the pass road

missions.title: Lost on the Tannberg
missions.brief: Nils Brandt, 34, skied off the back of the Tannberg top station into the trees and has not come down. His phone is dead. His friends found one of his gloves by the lift. Get Koda on his scent.
missions.alert: A skier missed the last chair. Last seen at the top station heading for the trees.
missions.done: Nils is warm, splinted and eating soup. He says Koda is the best dog he has ever met.

objectives.text: Get to the Tannberg top station: up the run on the sled, or fly
Let Koda take the scent from the glove, then follow
Warm Nils up and splint his ankle
Bring the sled over and help Nils on
Take Nils down to the clinic in Hollin
Hand Nils over at the clinic

missions.title: Firewood for the Kettle
missions.brief: Greta runs the Kettle, the lodge in Hollin. Her firewood and lamp oil came up on the truck and it's sitting in our yard. Snow's coming tonight: get it down to her.
missions.alert: Kessel Patrol, it's Greta at the Kettle. I'm down to my last logs and there's snow on the way.
missions.done: That's the stove sorted for a week. Come in for a hot chocolate any time.

objectives.text: Load the supply crate onto the sled rack
Get on the sled
Ride down to the Kettle in Hollin
Unload the crate for Greta

missions.title: Where's Pepper?
missions.brief: Pepper, Greta's grey cat, slipped out this morning and hasn't come back. She likes the old boathouse by Mirror Lake. Koda knows cats.
missions.alert: It's Greta again. Pepper went out before the snow and she hasn't come home.
missions.done: Pepper is on the windowsill pretending none of this happened.

objectives.text: Go to Mirror Lake
Show Koda the paw prints, then follow
Coax Pepper down and pick her up
Bring Pepper home to the Kettle
Give Pepper back to Greta

missions.title: Kessel Bowl Has Reloaded
missions.brief: The bowl has loaded up again, and the wind decides where: snow settles in the lee, so it is not always A and C. Fly the bowl and read all four slopes; the loaded ones get flagged on the mountain and the map for the control team. You can skip the flight and judge the slopes yourself, but a charge on sound snow is a charge wasted.
missions.alert: New snow on Kessel Bowl and the wind has been at it. Which slopes are loaded today?
missions.done: Report filed. The loaded slopes are flagged for the control team.

objectives.text: Start the helicopter on the pad
Fly to Kessel Bowl
Scan the four slopes: nose on each one, close and low
Fly home and land on the pad

missions.title: Bring Down the Bowl
missions.brief: Close the pass road, climb to Kessel Ridge and charge the loaded slopes: the ones the recon flight flagged, or your own read if nobody has flown it. You choose which slopes to charge, then fire from safe ground. Pay goes by how much of the loaded snow comes down; a charge on a stable slope is wasted, and a clean read (every loaded slope, nothing else) earns a bonus.
missions.alert: Kessel Bowl is loaded above the pass road. Bring it down before it comes down on its own.
missions.done: Bowl is down and the road is open again. Good work up there.

objectives.text: Take the charges from the locker in the garage
Close the pass road at the barrier
Take the ridge track up to Kessel Ridge
Charge the slopes you judge loaded, then get clear and fire
Get clear of the slope, then fire the charges
Watch it run
Reopen the pass road

missions.title: Tree Down on the Pass
missions.brief: The snow load brought a big spruce down across the pass road. Nobody hurt, but nothing gets up or down until it is cleared.
missions.alert: A spruce has come down across the pass road below Kessel Bowl.
missions.done: Pass road clear. Thanks for the quick work.

objectives.text: Get to the fallen tree on the pass road
Cut the trunk and drag it clear

missions.title: Stuck in the Drift

missions.alert: A van has slid into a drift on the Tannberg road.
missions.done: Van is back on the road. The driver waved. Mostly.

Tannberg Village, the base area, is one planned town (see TOWN below): Main Street runs north from
the parking lot at the valley road up to the lift base plaza, with Patrol HQ and its vehicle yard on
the west side and Hollin, the guest village, on the east.

unclassified.doc:
`ahead`: how far past the character the camera aims, as a share of its distance. Aiming past
you rather than at you puts you in the lower third and shows the ground you are heading into.
`portrait`: how much further back the camera sits on a tall, narrow phone screen.

Which slopes the wind loads. Snow blows over the ridge and settles in the lee, so the wind
that came with the new snow decides which of the four slopes carry slab. One of these per
reload, picked by the day.
The guns: where they stand and how far they reach (m).
Multipliers on the light that falls on snow (linear rgb): [lit, shade].

The people's night light (Field Guide Alpine, src/render/fieldGuide.ts): a cold fill on their colours
and a rim from the sky round their edges, both zero by day, so at night a figure stays readable
against moonlit snow without the night itself getting any brighter. Set by the rig.

Each piece's footprint (its own frame, metres) and how it meets the ground. `rules` say what ground it
can stand on when its spot is chosen; `drape` is how high (local y) the ground snow it carries reaches:
those parts are laid onto the terrain under them rather than left flat.

The ground: snow that is a little blue in the shade and warm in the sun, wind-scoured rock on
the steeps, packed roads, groomed pistes and the lake's grey ice. Drawn in chunks so the ones
behind you are culled; a ring of far peaks closes the valley.
Hand-placed patrol props: a rescue toboggan at the station, the lift top and the base; rescue caches where trouble happens; lanterns by doors.
Where things are inside and around the station.

levelcraft.title: LEVELCRAFT

findings.title: 56% of the mapped area holds nothing to find or do
findings.summary: Dividing the playable extent (1720×1192 units) into a 6×6 grid, 20 cells contain no placed location and no mission target; the emptiest quarter is the south-west (6 of 9 cells empty).
findings.why: Players read empty space as either a promise or a waste. Without a landmark, a cache or a reason to cross it, a large empty area becomes travel time between the parts of the game that matter.

findings.title: 37 of 58 named places are never a mission destination

findings.why: Named places are authored promises. When no objective, story beat or reward points at them, most players never discover they exist, and the world feels smaller than the map.

findings.title: Buying everything costs 5.6× what the campaign pays
findings.summary: The non-repeating missions pay 1390 funds in total; the 38 priced unlocks cost 7750. The gap is meant to be filled by 4 repeatable mission(s) (Kessel Bowl Has Reloaded, Bring Down the Bowl, Tree Down on the Pass and Stuck in the Drift).
findings.why: A large gap between income and prices turns the late game into grinding. If repeatable content fills it, that content carries the game's pacing and must be the best-designed part.

Both choices complete the mission; each changes the reward and a later line.
drift.experience: The mission becomes a story the player authored.
tradeoffs: Two outcomes to write and test.

validation.method: Playtest: which option did players pick and why?

drift.proposal: Invert Stuck in the Drift: the player causes the problem the mission normally solves, then deals with it.
changes: Start with the player's action triggering the situation; the rest of the mission is the consequence.
tradeoffs: Tone shift; must fit the fiction.
